title: Dimension at a closed point of a finite type algebra over a field is the dimension of the local ring
statement: Let $k$ be a field, $S$ a finitely generated $k$-algebra (a quotient of a polynomial ring $k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]) and $\mathfrak m\subset S$ a maximal ideal, with localization $S_{\mathfrak m}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Then the Krull dimension of the topological space $\operatorname{Spec}S$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] at the point $\mathfrak m$ [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point] equals the Krull dimension of the ring $S_{\mathfrak m}$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring].

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00OU (label lemma-dimension-closed-point-finite-type-field, line 27855), whose proof is 'a special case of' Lemma Tag 00OT (label lemma-dimension-at-a-point-finite-type-over-field, line 27787, equality of (1) and (3) for p = m); tags verified in stacks-project/tags/tags

proof.text: Write $X=\operatorname{Spec}S$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] and $V(I)=\{\mathfrak p\in X:I\subseteq\mathfrak p\}$ for an ideal $I\subseteq S$; these are the closed subsets of $X$. The field $k$ is a Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] (its only ideals are $0$ and $k$), so the finite type $k$-algebra $S$ is Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian], hence has only finitely many minimal prime ideals $\mathfrak q_1,\ldots,\mathfrak q_r$ [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finitely-many-minimal-primes]. Since $\mathfrak m$ is a prime ideal, $S\neq0$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma 00OT (lemma-dimension-at-a-point-finite-type-over-field, lines 27803-27852), specialized to the maximal ideal p = m as Lemma 00OU says: 'There are finitely many of them (see Lemmas 00FN lemma-obvious-Noetherian and 00FR lemma-Noetherian-topology)'

proof.text: Every open subset $W\subseteq X$ with $\mathfrak m\in W$ contains every prime ideal $\mathfrak p\subseteq\mathfrak m$ of $S$: by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-irreducible-closed-subsets-primes] (1), $\mathfrak m\in V(\mathfrak p)=\overline{\{\mathfrak p\}}$, so the open neighbourhood $W$ of $\mathfrak m$ meets $\{\mathfrak p\}$, i.e. $\mathfrak p\in W$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma 00OT (lemma-dimension-at-a-point-finite-type-over-field, lines 27803-27852), specialized to the maximal ideal p = m as Lemma 00OU says: the point x lies in every open W considered there, and the irreducible components of W are the Z_i meeting W

proof.text: Lower bound: $\dim W\ge\dim(S_{\mathfrak m})$ for every open $W\subseteq X$ with $\mathfrak m\in W$, where $\dim W$ is the Krull dimension of $W$ with the subspace topology [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Let $\mathfrak p_0\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq\mathfrak p_t$ be a chain of primes of $S$ with $\mathfrak p_t\subseteq\mathfrak m$. By step 2 every $\mathfrak p_j$ lies in $W$. Put $Y_j=V(\mathfrak p_j)\cap W$. The closure of $\{\mathfrak p_j\}$ in the subspace $W$ is $\overline{\{\mathfrak p_j\}}\cap W=V(\mathfrak p_j)\cap W=Y_j$ [lem-weil-pbc-spec-irreducible-closed-subsets-primes] (1); so $Y_j$ is closed in $W$, and irreducible as the closure in $W$ of the irreducible one-point set $\{\mathfrak p_j\}$ [lem-weil-pbc-irreducible-closure]. We have $Y_t\subseteq\cdots\subseteq Y_0$ since $V(\mathfrak p_{j+1})\subseteq V(\mathfrak p_j)$, and the inclusions are strict: $\mathfrak p_j\in Y_j$ but $\mathfrak p_j\notin V(\mathfrak p_{j+1})$ because $\mathfrak p_{j+1}\not\subseteq\mathfrak p_j$. So $Y_t\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq Y_0$ is a chain of irreducible closed subsets of $W$ of length $t$, and $\dim W\ge t$. Taking the supremum over all such chains, $\dim W\ge\dim(S_{\mathfrak m})$ by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-dimension-chains-below-prime].

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma 00OT (lemma-dimension-at-a-point-finite-type-over-field, lines 27803-27852), specialized to the maximal ideal p = m as Lemma 00OU says: 'there is a chain of irreducible closed subsets of length equal to dim(Z_i) in the open W_i'; here the point m itself is a closed point of each W_i, so the Jacobson property used there for a general p is not needed, and the chain is taken directly below m

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma 00OT (lemma-dimension-at-a-point-finite-type-over-field, lines 27803-27852), specialized to the maximal ideal p = m as Lemma 00OU says: 'Let I' = {i | x in Z_i}, and let T = union of the Z_i, i not in I'. Then U = X minus T is an open subset of X containing the point x.' (Z_i = V(q_i), Lemma 00ES (3))

proof.text: Upper bound: $\dim U\le\dim(S_{\mathfrak m})$. Let $Y_0\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq Y_t$ be a chain of irreducible closed subsets of $U$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Each $Y_j$ is irreducible also as a subset of $X$ (its subspace topology from $U$ and from $X$ agree), so its closure $\overline{Y_j}$ in $X$ is irreducible [lem-weil-pbc-irreducible-closure] and closed. Since $Y_j$ is closed in $U$, $Y_j=F\cap U$ for a closed $F\subseteq X$, so $\overline{Y_j}\subseteq F$ and $\overline{Y_j}\cap U=Y_j$; hence $\overline{Y_0}\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq\overline{Y_t}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-irreducible-closed-subsets-primes] (2) there are primes $P_j$ with $\overline{Y_j}=V(P_j)$, and by its part (1) the strict inclusions give $P_t\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq P_0$. By [lem-weil-pbc-prime-contains-minimal-prime] (with $I=0$) $P_t$ contains a minimal prime $\mathfrak q$ of $S$, which is one of $\mathfrak q_1,\ldots,\mathfrak q_r$ (step 1). As $Y_t\neq\emptyset$ (irreducible sets are nonempty) and $Y_t\subseteq V(P_t)\subseteq V(\mathfrak q)$, the set $V(\mathfrak q)$ meets $U$, so by step 4 $\mathfrak q=\mathfrak q_i$ with $i\in I'$, i.e. $\mathfrak q\subseteq\mathfrak m$. Now let $\bar S=S/\mathfrak q$: an integral domain ($\mathfrak q$ is prime), a finite type $k$-algebra (the composite of a surjection $k[x_1,\dots,x_n]\to S$ with $S\to\bar S$ is surjective) [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], with the maximal ideal $\bar{\mathfrak m}=\mathfrak m/\mathfrak q$. The primes of $\bar S$ are the $P/\mathfrak q$ for the primes $P\supseteq\mathfrak q$ of $S$, with inclusions preserved (correspondence of ideals of a quotient, and $\bar S/(P/\mathfrak q)\cong S/P$). So $P_t/\mathfrak q\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq P_0/\mathfrak q$ is a chain of primes of $\bar S$ and $t\le\dim\bar S$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-domain-dimension-local-ring], $\dim\bar S=\dim(\bar S_{\bar{\mathfrak m}})$, and by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-dimension-chains-below-prime] the latter is the supremum of the lengths $s$ of chains $P'_0\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq P'_s\subseteq\bar{\mathfrak m}$ of primes of $\bar S$. Each such chain is the image of a chain of primes $\mathfrak q\subseteq P''_0\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq P''_s\subseteq\mathfrak m$ of $S$, so $s\le\dim(S_{\mathfrak m})$ by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-dimension-chains-below-prime] applied to $S$ and $\mathfrak m$. Hence $t\le\dim(S_{\mathfrak m})$ for every chain, i.e. $\dim U\le\dim(S_{\mathfrak m})$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma 00OT (lemma-dimension-at-a-point-finite-type-over-field, lines 27803-27852), specialized to the maximal ideal p = m as Lemma 00OU says: 'For any open W in U with x in W the irreducible components of W are the W_i = Z_i cap W for i in I'', 'Since W_i in Z_i we have dim(W_i) <= dim(Z_i)', and 'the dimension of S_m is the maximum of the dimensions of the Z_i passing through x_0' via Lemma 00OS (lemma-dimension-spell-it-out); here x_0 = x = m

proof.text: Conclusion. By definition [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point], $\dim_{\mathfrak m}X$ is the minimum of $\dim W$ over the open $W\ni\mathfrak m$. Step 3 gives $\dim W\ge\dim(S_{\mathfrak m})$ for all of them, and the open $U\ni\mathfrak m$ of step 4 has $\dim U\le\dim(S_{\mathfrak m})$ by step 5. Hence $\dim_{\mathfrak m}X=\dim U=\dim(S_{\mathfrak m})$.
